goal: Help a home cook capture first, see automatic organization succeed, build trustworthy cooking-event history, improve a dish cover safely, and plan one or more dishes for any selected day.

requirements.description: Plan and Menu keep the stable floating Plan–capture–Menu shell, with no permanent Capture or Review tab and no competing empty-state capture button.

Plan uses a selected-day view where one date can contain multiple dishes, one clear add action targets that date, a visually separate recommendation is explicitly not planned, and an empty non-today date has the same add path.
The calendar shows all seven days, visually distinguishes today from the selected date, exposes previous/next week controls, and demonstrates reaching a date outside the current week.

A planned dish row visibly opens details, its secondary action exposes Move to another day and Remove from plan, and removal remains reversible through a compact temporary Undo toast fixed above—not covering—the bottom navigation.

Take Photo captures without classification, confirms immediate local save while AI organizes, then visibly demonstrates both automatic existing-dish matching and new-dish creation with Correct and Undo paths.
Offline capture remains locally queued with a clear later-organizing state, while denied camera permission preserves Import Photos and Add Idea alternatives and explains the Settings recovery path.

Capture offers Take Photo, Import Photos, and Add Idea before any destination decision; Add Idea captures only a dish idea and optional memory note, with no planning controls, and has canonical valid and retained-content validation states.
Review remains contextual, uses unambiguous progress wording, supports existing-dish and new-dish outcomes, and demonstrates an empty alternate-dish search with clear query correction.

Dish Detail presents Improve Cover as a persistent compact chip on the cover image; the flow explains that sources inform a new cover without changing originals, supports source selection and optional freeform visual direction, shows generation, compares current and proposed covers, and requires Use this cover or Keep current.
Offline and online-generation failure states both preserve the current cover and local dish knowledge, distinguish their causes, and provide non-destructive retry or exit paths.

Cook Again explains whether the user is cooking now or planning for later; made count represents cooking occasions, source-photo count is distinct, and multiple photos can appear inside one dated cooking occasion.

The single filterable Menu grid and the first Dish Detail viewport surface cooking-history, source, favorite, or latest-note cues so the product reads as a living cooking memory rather than a generic recipe library.

Menu labels the collection as 24 dishes, uses All, Favorites, Recently added, and Filters to control one unified dish grid without duplicate Favorites and All sections, and covers a search-empty state with concise query-clearing guidance.
The empty Menu relies on the persistent global capture button as its only dominant action and uses capture-first language rather than manual filing language.
Every delivery screen retains the shared cream, orange, charcoal, soft-surface, high-radius, rounded-type, and ambient-shadow system with one dominant filled action per task region.

Seven-day calendars, multiple planned dishes, long names, grouped history, comparison states, bottom actions, and recovery copy remain readable and reachable on iPhone SE, iPhone 14, and Pixel 7 without clipped or covered controls.
